<page>
Harbor Point Mutual Auto Insurance
Bodily Injury Unit
Claim Notes
Claim number:
C-1322
Claimant:
Natasha Jimenez
Adjuster:
Darin Tyler
2024-03-29
Claim received for a rear-end collision in which the insured's vehicle was struck from behind while stopped at a traffic
signal. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by an attorney.
2024-04-25
Reviewed the policy and confirmed the driver of the insured vehicle is named on the policy and coverage was in force
at the time of loss.
2024-05-24
Obtained photographs of both vehicles. The rear damage is mostly consistent with the impact described, though a
few old scratches on the bumper may predate this crash and are being noted separately.
2024-06-09
Statements from two witnesses and the other driver all match the account of how the collision occurred. Nothing so
far suggests the damage hpapened before coverage began.
2024-06-20
Claimant joined the claim several days after the incident. No one at the scene recorded the claimant's name, so the
claimant's presence in the vehicle is being confirmed throguh the other driver and witness accounts.
2024-08-14
Claimant's description of events has been the same in every conversation so far. The reported shoulder injury is
plausible for a collision of this type.
2024-09-15
Claimant disclosed a samll strain to the same area several years ago, which healed fully according to prior records.
Noted for the file and will be considered in evaluating the current injury.
2024-11-07
Treatment followed a usual course for this type of injury and tapered off as the claimant improved. Records show
steady progress with fewer visits over the last several weeks.
2024-11-15
File summary: liability is clear, the reported injury is consistent with the mechanism of impact, and treatment has
tapered as expected. Recommending continued handling of the injury component on the standard timeline.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- occurrence_support: Do independent sources (witnesses, photos, cameras, the other driver) confirm that the accident happened as described? Allowed: Confirmed, Partially corroborated, Uncorroborated, Contradicted, Suspected staged.
- damage_crash_fit: Does the vehicle damage fit the described impact? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- account_stability: Did the claimant's account of the accident stay the same over time? Allowed: Stable, Clarified, Materially changed.
- occupant_presence: Was the claimant really in the vehicle at the time of the crash? Allowed: Verified, Unclear, Added later, Not present.
- prior_damage_evidence: Is there evidence of vehicle damage from before this crash? Allowed: None, Possible, Documented, Material.
- known_loss_evidence: Is there evidence the damage existed or was known before the coverage started? Allowed: Weak, Moderate, Strong.
- driver_status: Is the driver of the insured vehicle on the policy? Allowed: Listed, Household, Unlisted, Excluded.

For each rated feature give:
- "rating": exactly one of the allowed ratings,
- "confidence": "High", "Medium" or "Low" (how clearly the page shows it),
- "quote": one or two sentences copied EXACTLY from the page that support the rating, with any
  spelling errors as they are,
- "reason": one short sentence.
JSON format:
